claim: At R40H400, independent reruns disagree on 3.83 to 4.38 of 6 qualifiers in these controlled fields.
reason: Tight intervals in all three fields; replicated by the independent 200-tournament mu_swiss sample.

claim: 2.74 to 3.80 of the selected six are outside the mu_field reference top 6 at R40H400.
reason: All fields; consistent against mu_swiss reference; robust to reference propagation.

claim: In the engineered separated control, each validated leader qualifies with probability 0.31 to 0.76, and the exact top 6 was selected in 2 of 250 tournaments.
reason: Wilson intervals from 200 tournaments; leaders independently validated.

claim: Reliability improves continuously with rounds, with no evidence of a plateau within the preregistered 40-round horizon.
reason: Monotone at every step on every metric in every field.

claim: At an equal scheduled hand budget, ten 1,600-hand rounds select less reliably than forty 400-hand rounds in all three controlled fields.
reason: Paired contrasts exclude zero on rerun changed qualifiers and regret in every field.

claim: In the source-schedule counterfactual, adaptive Swiss is more consistent than a frozen replay of its own schedule in all three controlled fields.
reason: Changed-qualifier and rerun rank-correlation contrasts exclude zero in every field.

claim: Most wrong qualifiers are bots the mu_field reference clearly places outside the top 6.
reason: Shares 1.00, 0.80, 0.79; regret tracks wrong count (r 0.90, 0.79, 0.79).

claim: Reference uncertainty is small relative to tournament noise, and the mu_field and mu_swiss references order the bots almost identically.
reason: Self-regret median <= 2.7 BB (97.5 percentile <= 10.7) vs tournament regret >= 94 BB; Spearman >= 0.97; no significant discordant pairs.

claim: Twenty 800-hand rounds perform close to forty 400-hand rounds.
reason: Intervals include zero except style_diverse changed qualifiers (0.34 [0.05, 0.62]); absence of difference is not equivalence.

claim: Part of the R10H1600 deficit persists at matched played hands.
reason: Holds in separated_control (both metrics) and style_diverse (regret, wrong vs mu_field); inconclusive in crowded_cutoff; post hoc descriptive.

claim: Adaptive pairing reduces regret relative to the frozen replay.
reason: Clear in separated_control and crowded_cutoff; style_diverse regret −11.6 [−24.7, 1.1] includes zero.

claim: The short-match six-lane duplicate package is more consistent than ordinary play.
reason: Rerun Spearman higher in all three fields; changed-qualifier and regret contrasts negative everywhere but individually clear only in separated_control; package comparison.

claim: The fewer-rounds six-lane duplicate package helps in the crowded-cutoff field.
reason: Only that field (−0.49 [−0.78, −0.20]); not in the other two.

claim: Duplication helps only when lanes stay coupled (short matches).
reason: Mechanistic reading consistent with bust rates and played-hand ratios; not tested directly.

claim: Tournament noise per bot is about as large as the between-bot strength spread inside Swiss.
reason: Descriptive approximation in this dossier (Section 4.11); not a preregistered analysis.

claim: The separated control has the costliest errors.
reason: True for regret per wrong qualifier, but driven by its engineered gap; regret is not comparable across fields.

claim: Swiss is unreliable in general.
reason: One frozen field per scenario; synthetic agents; research semantics.

claim: 40 rounds are insufficient in general.
reason: Only these fields; no external target reliability; no horizon beyond 40.

claim: The tournament fails to recover true skill.
reason: References are mechanism-specific estimands; no true skill ranking exists in the design.

claim: Compute was held fixed in Experiment B.
reason: Only scheduled hands were equal; played fractions 0.57 / 0.80 / 0.94; runtime throttled.

claim: Adaptive Swiss causally improves selection.
reason: Experiment C is a source-schedule counterfactual with inherited adaptive schedules and fresh randomness.

claim: Duplication causally reduces variance.
reason: Experiment D packages also change rounds or match length.

claim: The separated control is representative.
reason: Engineered from the strongest six plus the 54 weakest pool bots.

claim: R10 is worse at equal played hands everywhere.
reason: Inconclusive in crowded_cutoff; identity metric inconclusive in style_diverse.

claim: Reliability plateaus at some number of rounds, or N more rounds would reach a target.
reason: No plateau observed and no data beyond 40 rounds.

claim: Selection errors are mainly near-equal swaps at the cutoff.
reason: About four in five (all, in the separated control) are clearly weaker bots.

claim: Crowded fields (or diverse fields) require X rounds.
reason: No regime-level inference from one field per scenario.

claim: Results describe historical FullHouse events or any future competition format.
reason: Research semantics only; no future-format statements.

claim: High-variance styles systematically over-qualify relative to their strength.
reason: Archetype residuals are small and change sign across fields; not analysed as a hypothesis.

claim: Short duplication significantly improves selection in every field.
reason: Individually clear only in separated_control on qualifier and regret contrasts.
